description: I am requesting an Inspectional Services inspection regarding an ongoing mouse infestation in my apartment at 68 Myrtle Street, Unit 7, Boston, MA. The mouse issue has been ongoing for more than three weeks. I have notified both the landlord and property management company, and exterminators have been to the apartment on multiple occasions; however, the problem has not been resolved. I have personally taken additional measures in an effort to prevent mice from entering the apartment, including placing steel wool in crevices and openings throughout the unit where mice may be able to gain access.  I have also observed mice in the laundry area in the basement of the building. This raises concern that the rodent issue may extend beyond my individual apartment and that there may be building-wide conditions contributing to the infestation. I have been informed that Quality Services, the property management company, was expected to inspect the apartment, including pulling out the dishwasher to access the wall, identify and seal holes or cracks that could provide mouse access into the unit, and replace the existing traps. I was told this work would be completed by the end of the day on September 17, but the work was not completed as communicated. I have continued communicating with the landlord and property management company and have made repeated efforts to address the issue. I am requesting an Inspectional Services inspection to determine whether there are housing, maintenance, or structural conditions allowing rodents to enter and remain in the apartment and what corrective action is necessary. Given the continued sightings in both the apartment and the building's basement laundry area, this appears to be an ongoing infestation and not an isolated rodent sighting.

description:
Christopher Columbus Park (Atlantic Ave, North End/Waterfront) is being badly damaged by off-leash dogs. Since the end of summer, dog owners have been letting their dogs run loose across the main lawn every day. The damage is severe and getting worse.

At least 60% of the grass has been worn down. You can clearly see the paths and loops where dogs run, and those areas are now brown, gray, and bare dirt. This is the same lawn that residents and visitors sit on all summer, and it's one of the most visible parks in the city. Right now it looks neglected and reflects poorly on Boston.

Requesting the following:

	1.	Post clear "Dogs must be leashed" signs at every entrance to the lawn.
	2.	Increase enforcement of the leash ordinance by Park Rangers and/or police, especially mornings and evenings when off-leash activity peaks.
	3.	Assess and repair the lawn (reseeding or sod) before the damage becomes permanent.

This needs prompt attention. Without signage and enforcement, the remaining grass will be lost.

description:
-- auto translated (en-US) -- We parked at the lot at McKinley Preparatory High School on Friday, 9/25. An attendant took $60 cash from us at 5pm. When we returned at 9pm our car, and at least five others, were blocked by a second row of cars. No attendant was available. We called the tow company whose name was on the school building. They informed us that we were likely scammed and that they could not help us. They mentioned that this is an on-going issue and suggested that we “make a ruckus” because someone from the school will likely come outside to investigate at which point we could instruct them to call the towing company on our behalf (the towing company can’t tow anyone without permission from the school, which owns the lot). We waited for HOURS, with fifteen in our party trapped and several in other cars also trapped and angry. The police would not help because it’s a private lot. description: On Friday evening, September 26th, 2026 at approximately 9:45pm, my husband, a cyclist on his commute home from his job in the Seaport was doored, resulting in bodily injuries and with the bike so damaged, he couldn't ride it home. The bike is currently at the bike repair shop. I'm incensed as this is the 2nd time in a year this has happened to him. The stretch of Seaport Blvd from the Moakley Bridge to the Leader Bank Pavilion, both sides, is dangerous for cyclists as cars routinely park in the bike lanes, forcing riders out into the traffic. Ride share drivers routinely pull over to pick up and drop off passengers and it's the disembarking passengers who cause the most damage as they cannot see behind them and open their doors rapidly, causing accidents like the one my husband suffered. When I came to pick up my injured husband and his damaged bike, there were 2 Boston Police cruisers on scene, with blue lights flashing as they documented the scene. Astonishingly, despite the flashing blue lights, a driver pulled over and blocked the bike lane in front of us. That's how common and blatant this practice is. I realize this is not a quick fix issue, but something needs to change and I beg of you not to wait until someone is killed to be the catalyst for change. Ideally, we'd have a protected bike lane. But for now, the situation is dangerous and untenable. What is needed right now is constant heavy enforcement from either parking officers to aggressively ticket to visible police presence to keep everyone where they belong. A short term solution could be the creation of designated pick up and drop off zones for ride shares and their pick up and delivery counterparts. Please take this seriously. My husband is alive and his bike is in the shop, hopefully repairable and I consider us lucky. Please don't let my husband or any one else be the ultimate victim in order to force a change of ways in this area.

description:
I have been in contact with the NPS and our Charlestown Representative about having a public trash receptacle installed along 5th street in the Charlestown Navy Yard. To recap my conversation with NPS and others, we have seen a large amount of trash being left in the bushes and green space between the ropewalk building and our building (Muster House, 31 5th street). Over the past year. On average we collect a 50-gallon trash bin worth of debris that have been left in the area on  bi-weekly to monthly basis. This has previously included hazardous trash like needles etc and nips, food trash, etc. We have been working to keep this area clean ourselves, but it is becoming increasingly difficult with summer camps and others leaving trash in the area as they enter and exit the Navy Yard on our property. We also do not have anywhere to put a dumpster so disposal is very difficult to deal with. 
 
I would like to work the city to have a trash can installed on 5th street to alleviate these issues. Currently, the closest public trash is available across 1st Ave, adjacent to Dry Dock 2. We would be happy to assist with the cost of installation if the helps move things along. I have attached a photograph showing a potential install location that would see most of the foot traffic entering and exiting the Navy Yard passing by it. Please let me know if you have any questions or how we can work on moving this forward. 
 
Thank you for your assistance with this matter. 
 
Thanks, Graham
 
Graham Velji
Building Enclosure Associates, LLC
Charlestown Navy Yard
31 Fifth Street
Boston, MA 02129

Good morning,

I am submitting this report to bring attention to the large trees that are falling and creating a potential safety hazard along Neponset Valley Parkway, particularly between 209 and 239 Neponset Valley Parkway.

I am also requesting that the tree limbs and branches in front of 229 and 239 Neponset Valley Parkway be properly cut back and removed where necessary.

The safety of residents and their homes is very important, and I respectfully ask that this matter be inspected and addressed as soon as possible.

Respectfully,
Concern citizen of the Commonwealth.

I am reporting an ongoing illegal dumping and public safety concern at 1333 Blue Hill Ave, Mattapan, MA 02126, directly across from the BGCB Teen Center at 10 Hazelton St., Mattapan, MA 02126.

The attached photographs document significant debris and waste around the property, including multiple large trash bags, loose litter, discarded materials, and several large barrels/containers with unknown contents. The conditions appear unsanitary and create a potential health, safety, and environmental hazard, particularly given the location directly across from a youth/community center.

There is also substantial litter and debris along the sidewalk/grass strip adjacent to the property, contributing to an unsightly and potentially unsafe pedestrian environment.

As a disappointed homeowner and active member of the Mattapan community, I am asking the City to please:

    Inspect the property and surrounding area.

    Determine whether the dumped materials and barrels are being stored or disposed of legally.

    Remove the illegally dumped debris and waste, if appropriate.

    Investigate whether the barrels contain hazardous or unknown substances.

    Address the accumulated litter along the public sidewalk/grass strip.

    Take appropriate enforcement action if violations are found.

This condition is particularly concerning because it is directly across from a teen/community center and is visible to residents, pedestrians, and young people using the area.

Please document this complaint, inspect the location, and provide a case number and follow-up regarding what action will be taken.

Thank you for addressing this matter and helping maintain a clean and safe Mattapan community.

I’m writing regarding the overnight construction at 255 St. Botolph St.
I am aware that this overnight construction has a permit from the city, and am asking you to reevaluate that because I believe it is based on a wrong and unethical evaluation of priority.
I heard that the city gave permission for overnight constructions because they cannot afford to close down the street during the day.
1. About 5 cars use the street per minute during the day, not as many as your everyday street.
2. Bigger streets like Huntington Ave have been fully or partially shut down in the past due to construction, according to my knowledge.
3. As long as you place the signs in the right places, the drivers lose only two minutes or so taking a detour through another street.
4. Even if you don’t place the signs in the right places (which I trust will not be the case) the drivers lose only five minutes or so.
5. This is a residential street, with NEC and northeastern dorms, and the NEC residence has I believe around or over 300 people living there. These people lose hours of sleep, and it’s been happening for a month. That causes health issues. Shutting down the street during the day doesn’t.
Please reevaluate accordingly and escalate this issue if you can’t do anything about it.

Additionally, the asphalt repair was supposed to be temporary and was to be replaced with concrete. That has still not been done. As a result, pieces of asphalt continue to break apart and become lodged in my lawn mower and snow blower.

I am respectfully requesting that this matter finally be addressed and properly resolved. After more than five years of waiting, I believe it is reasonable to expect that the original issues be corrected and the damage to my property be repaired.

A townhouse is undergoing a gut renovation (16 Rutland sq apt 1 boston). Our buildings date to approximately 1860. Over the last several days, during construction activity, our indoor air-quality monitors have repeatedly measured PM2.5 above 200 micrograms per cubic meter. Our normal indoor level is generally 5 or below, and we have never seen readings remotely this high before.  They correspond to when our neighbors are doing construction, and we do not see any barriers in place.  

We’re concerned that construction dust is migrating from the renovation into our home. We have young children in the house. Given the age of the buildings, we’re also concerned about whether appropriate lead-safe renovation and dust-containment procedures are being followed.

We’d like to have the appropriate city department inspect the construction site and determine whether the contractor is using required containment and whether the work is being performed in compliance with applicable permits and safety requirements.

description:
Good afternoon,

I am reaching out because I am desperately trying to find help for two elderly family members who have been living with an ongoing bed bug issue in their apartment since November.

Their property management company has been made aware of the problem and treatments have been performed, but unfortunately, the issue has still not been resolved. They continue to find what appear to be bed bugs in their home, including in their bedding, along with blood spotting. I have attached recent photographs to document what they are continuing to experience.

At this point, I am extremely concerned about their well-being. My aunt is elderly, diabetic, and already dealing with complications related to her health. Both residents are in delicate health, and having to continuously live and sleep in these conditions for nearly a year is taking a serious toll on them physically and emotionally.

They have tried to work through the appropriate channels and have exhausted the options available to them through the property, yet they are still living with this problem. They are becoming increasingly depressed and isolated. Family and friends are understandably afraid to visit because of the possibility of bringing bed bugs back into their own homes. It is heartbreaking to watch two elderly people become isolated in their own home because an infestation has been allowed to continue for this long.

I understand that bed bugs can be difficult to eradicate and may require multiple treatments. However, asking elderly residents with existing medical conditions to simply continue living in an infested apartment while repeated treatments fail is not an acceptable long-term solution.

I am asking for someone to please intervene and help us determine what can be done immediately. If the apartment requires more extensive treatment, we would like assistance determining whether they can be temporarily relocated to a safe place while the unit is properly treated and cleared, with the ability to return to their home afterward. If that is not possible, we need guidance on what other housing or enforcement resources are available to them.

We are not asking for special treatment. We are asking for a safe and sanitary home for two elderly people who have already been dealing with this for far too long.

Please let me know who I should speak with, what documentation you need from us, or what steps we need to take to have this situation formally reviewed. I am happy to provide records of previous treatments, communications with management, additional photographs, or any other information that may help.

I would greatly appreciate a response as soon as possible. They need help, and after nearly a year of living with this, I do not believe it is reasonable or humane for them to continue waiting for the situation to improve on its own.

Thank you for taking the time to read this and for any assistance you can provide.

description: Resubmitted from mobile case BCS-00339535: "I am requesting a housing inspection for ongoing water intrusion and unresolved leaks at 254 Newbury St., Unit 6. There are currently three known leaks: two bedroom window leaks and a living-room ceiling leak. One of the bedroom window leaks has been reported to my property management company repeatedly over the past several months, but the underlying issue has not been repaired. Following the major storm last weekend, two additional leaks occurred. I reported all three leaks to management on Sunday, September 27. Maintenance came on Monday, September 28, but no permanent repair was made. I was provided with a bucket and told that management was waiting for a contractor. description:
19 Faraday Street Hyde Park Ma

Location has been reported before & inspectional services and also EMS dispatched on a wellness check.  Elderly woman removed from property.
Walking dog this morning and front door open.   Horrible smell coming from house.   Can see trash and litter in living room.  There have been rodents seen in yard.

When walking at the commonwealth ave mall around 9:50 am on Friday 10/2 (near comm ave and Gloucester intersection in back bay), I was hit by a rock from a Cambridge Landscaping industrial lawnmower. The lawnmower was on the comm ave mall and too close to pedestrians; as a result of this, a rock was propelled by the lawnmower and hit my ear, knocking my ear pod out. This caused immediate pain in my ear. It could have hit my eye and additional safety measures need to be implemented  to prevent future incidents. 

The man operating the lawnmower  was very resistant to identifying himself, and was hassling me when I called 911 to ask about an accident report. Which is why I took the attached picture. My ear hurt on impact and was red, but was not bleeding. I wanted to have a record of what happened in case I had an injury that required treatment. This is analgous to what you do with a car accident. The man operating the lawnmower became very adversarial and took a picture of me. I'm a female who was by myself walking two dogs and this behavior made me very uncomfortable.

The man operating the lawn mower was operating a Cambridge landscaping vest, and showed me the contact info for his manager. I took a photo of that contact info and attaching here, along with a picture of the lawnmower.

Having landscapers driving without care and so close to pedestrians is unsafe. If the city is hiring landscapers, they clearly need better supervision and instruction. There should  also be a complaint process and safety reporting process. The man who caused the accident was giving me the runaround and became very oppositional. As a resident of back bay and attorney. I was very upset and wouldn’t want this to happen to someone else; someone operating this negligently could really hurt someone and this a liability for the city.

The property at 97 Greenfield Rd, directly next to 101 Greenfield Rd, has been severely overgrown and appears to have been unmaintained for an extended period of time.

There are multiple large, mature trees immediately along the property line. Their branches extend toward the neighboring property, including toward our garage and house. A large branch from one of these trees has previously fallen onto our garage and caused physical damage, including a hole in the garage structure. There is concern that additional branches could fall and cause further property damage or potentially create a safety hazard.

The property is also heavily overgrown with substantial vegetation, weeds, dead growth, and accumulated debris throughout the yard. Vegetation is growing along and through the chain-link fence and up toward the sidewalk. The condition of the property appears to require significant cleanup and maintenance.

The property has recently had activity after previously appearing vacant. Today, multiple moving trucks and police were present at the property, and people have been coming and going to perform work on the house. It is unclear who currently has responsibility for the property.

Please inspect the property and determine whether the current condition of the yard, vegetation, trees, and property maintenance complies with Boston’s requirements. Please also determine whether the mature trees/branches along the property line present a potential hazard given the previous damage to the neighboring garage.

Photographs documenting the current condition of the property, the trees, the overgrown vegetation, and the previous garage damage are available and can be provided.

Additional information

The neighboring property is 97 Greenfield Rd and my property is 101 Greenfield Rd. The concern is specifically the condition of the property and the mature trees along the shared property line. There has already been documented property damage from a fallen branch.

description: You recently installed a new traffic light at the corner of Hackensack Road and the West Roxbury Parkway near the roundabout.  This is a dangerous intersection and installing a light is probably a good idea.  However, for the third time in as many days, I just watched 3 cars run the red light coming from the rounadabout.  If the person on Hackensack Rd had pulled into the intersection on their green light, they would have been hit by the oncoming cars.  At the moment, the intersection is more dangerous than it was without a traffic light, since before the installation, those on Hackensack Rd had to be extra careful about pulling into the intersection.  I think you need to send someone out to monitor the new light and figure out how to make the cars coming off the roundabout pay attention to the new signal.  Otherwise it is a matter of days until there’s a really bad accident.  In the photo you can see the grey car approaching from the roundabout going through their red light (the green signal is for the car on Hackensack Rd).  At the very least, there should be signs in the roundabout and approaching the roundabout from all directions about the new set of lights.

description: Due to a blockage in our plumbing, plumbers came and inserted a snake into the drain. The snake become stuck either 8/17-8/18, so we could no longer use our bathrooms. We were told to use the gas station bathroom down the street. Then, upon them realizing that they could not easily fix the plumber’s mistake, placed porta potties in our garage 8/28 (as evidenced by screenshot with camera time stamp). We have had to use them since then. The drain hole with the snake is left uncovered, allowing sewage/blocked waste to waft into our building (this is connected to our break room where we eat). People often trip over the snake/open drain when walking to and from the break room. We have had to use these porta potties for over a month at this point with no indication of when our bathrooms will be worked on. The company this is at: Dutchess Cannabis on 259 Cambridge St, Allston, MA 02134. They are disgusting to use and are incredibly unsanitary, especially since our customers have access to them. Numerous coworkers refuse to use them and hold it until they are home, which is unreasonable to expect and a health hazard itself. We also have a pregnant coworker who has to use the bathroom often, so she should not have to be subjected to these unsanitary conditions. Frequently we’ve had customers comment on how unacceptable it is we have to use these at a business where indoor bathrooms are available, but they just won’t have it fixed. The company has dragged their feet on this for well over a month and it needs to be dealt with, especially as it gets colder.

We are hoping that a field maintenance staff can address the infield at Boston Common softball, as the infield could really benefit from being groomed/lined. Additionally, there are some patches of grass growing towards the outskirts of the infield. The grass patches become a safety concern, as ground balls take bad hops off these patches and can often lead to facial injuries among participants. Having this removed would also be greatly appreciated.

description:
Dear City of Boston Inspectional Services and Public Health Officials,

I am requesting a coordinated investigation of the dumpster operation at 51 Walnut Street in Dorchester, across from my home.

The pastor told me he receives $700 per month to keep these dumpsters on the property for a separate business. They appear to be used for outside waste rather than solely for the church’s own trash. I have attached a photograph showing mattresses piled above the rim of the container. This condition raises serious concerns about sanitation, pests, illegal dumping, fire safety, and whether the commercial use is properly authorized.

I previously reported the overflowing trash through Boston 311 under case BCS-00342234. I was told that the City could not take action because the property is private. However, private ownership should not prevent the City from reviewing possible public-health, sanitation, zoning, licensing, building, fire-safety, or environmental violations.

Please forward this complaint to, or coordinate with, all appropriate departments and agencies, including:

* Boston Inspectional Services Department, including Code Enforcement and Building/Zoning.
* Boston Public Health Commission, including Environmental Health.
* Boston 311 and the Mayor’s Office of Constituent Services.
* Boston Fire Department, if the dumpsters or stored materials create a fire or access hazard.
* Boston Water and Sewer Commission, if there is any concern about runoff, drainage, or contamination.
* The Massachusetts Department of Environmental Protection, if the operation involves regulated waste, illegal dumping, or environmental violations.
* Any other City or state agency with jurisdiction over commercial dumpster storage, waste hauling, sanitation, or land use.

Please arrange an on-site inspection and determine:

* Whether the property has the required Site Cleanliness License or other applicable license.
* Whether the dumpster-storage operation requires additional City or state permits.
* Whether the use is allowed at this property under applicable zoning and land-use rules.
* Whether the property owner, church, dumpster owner, or waste hauler is properly licensed.

I am writing to request an urgent review of the recent traffic signal timing change at the intersection of Summer Street and Dorchester Avenue near South Station.
The timing for vehicles turning left from Dorchester Avenue onto Summer Street appears to have been significantly shortened. Vehicles currently receive only approximately 7–10 seconds of green time to complete the left turn. Compounding this issue, the vehicle green phase begins only after the pedestrian walk phase, and pedestrians frequently have not cleared the crosswalk by the time vehicles receive their green. As a result, the already very short window for turning vehicles is effectively reduced even further.
This is creating significant and unnecessary congestion. Traffic is routinely unable to clear the intersection during the available green phase, causing vehicles to back up and contributing to gridlock in multiple directions around the intersection and the surrounding South Station area.
I understand that traffic signal timing needs to account for pedestrian safety and traffic flow in multiple directions. However, the current configuration does not appear to be functioning effectively for either purpose.

description:
I had a bad fall yesterday on the sidewalk on the west side of Harrison Avenue, just south of Perry Street. A paving stone was out of alignment by 2-3 inches. The city is resurfacing the street, and two city employees helped me up (I am 76 years old) spray-painted the offending stone orange, and said it should be fixed as soon as possible. The photos below show my eye and face injuries. My knee was also badly hurt, and walking is now painful. When I fell, the stone was NOT yet painted orange! Photos below show it after your helpful guys sprayed it. 

You are resurfacing Harrison to make it safer for cars and cyclists, but how about pedestrians? I should be able to walk safely in my neighborhood. I will also context my city councillor. Please respond to this request.

Intersection of New Chardon, Congress, Merrimac Streets at One Congress St is a huge intersection. The pedestrian light cycle time is not nearly time to get through the cross walk to the other side. Additionally, drivers run the red lights and drive very fast all the time nearly striking pedestrians. There have been several people actually hit by cars.  There are thousands of people that work in the offices and court house at the intersection. 
 Please extend cross walk time and help us with the extreme safety issues.

​I am writing to formally voice my frustration regarding severe, ongoing maintenance issues in the building that are impacting all residents' health, safety, and daily living conditions.
​1. Trash Compactor Inoperable for Months
The trash compactor has been out of service for months. As a result, garbage is piling up, creating an unbearable stench throughout the building hallways and posing a clear sanitation hazard. This ongoing failure is unacceptable and places an unfair, excessive physical burden on our building's custodian, who is constantly forced to manually deal with the overflow.
​2. Severe Elevator Disruptions & Inspection Failures
For the past two weeks, only one elevator has been operational for the entire building. To make matters worse, the currently running elevator was previously shut down because it was overdue for a required safety inspection—an inspection it still has not received. It was simply turned back on because the other elevator broke down. Operating an uninspected elevator while leaving residents with unreliable access is a major safety and accessibility violation.
3. Inadequate On-Site Management
These persistent issues highlight a concerning pattern: building management continues to do the bare minimum rather than proactively resolving critical property problems. Passive oversight is no longer tolerable when basic basic amenities, cleanliness, and safety standards are being compromised.

description: Vehicles Blocking Safe Access to Residential Driveway I am requesting assistance with vehicles consistently parking too close to my residential driveway, making it extremely difficult and, at times, impossible to safely enter or exit my property. I own a large pickup truck, and the limited clearance caused by these parked vehicles makes maneuvering into and out of my driveway extremely challenging. On a recent occasion, I accidentally struck my own fence while attempting to enter my driveway because of the restricted turning space. This is an ongoing issue that interferes with my ability to safely access my property and creates a risk of additional property damage or vehicle collisions. I have attached photographs showing how closely these vehicles are parked to my driveway. I respectfully request that Boston Transportation Department Parking Enforcement inspect this location, address any vehicles parked illegally or obstructing driveway access, and evaluate whether additional parking restrictions or pavement markings are necessary to maintain safe driveway clearance. Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

DESCRIPTION / ISSUE DETAILS:
A vital reminder for all public service personnel regarding their foundational duties to serve the community dutifully, politely, and with deep empathy, patience, and understanding.
Public service requires a commitment to community care, infrastructure safety, and transparent engagement. The majority of times residents reach out to city departments, they are experiencing their most vulnerable moments or navigating highly upsetting and traumatic situations. Negative verbiage or raw frustration displayed by residents under stress is an expression of that vulnerability; public personnel must learn not to personalize this transferred stress, and they must utilize patience to de-escalate negativity to the absolute best of their ability.
Simultaneously, mutual respect is mandatory. Public servants are dedicated workers who do not deserve, nor do they need, to be disrespected, and the public must be reminded to remain respectful. Handling high-pressure moments with a calm, de-escalating posture preserves the dignity of both the worker and the citizen, keeping safety and equity at the center of all community interactions.
LOCATION OF INCIDENT:
Boston City Hall, 1 City Hall Square, Boston, MA 02201
SUBMITTED BY:
Anthony Meeks
Resident & Volunteer Community Advocate

description:
I’m submitting this because I’m very concerned about something I’ve repeatedly seen at Draper Pool over the past couple of weeks. I recently started bringing my child to swim team practice there, and on multiple occasions, I have seen the same lifeguard appearing to be asleep while working.

My family typically comes to the pool in the mornings or early afternoons, and we honestly fell in love with the facility this past summer. There are so many great things available for children, and we were really excited to have found a place where our kids could swim, participate in activities, and enjoy themselves. Unfortunately, this experience has been the complete opposite of what we expected and has made me seriously question whether I feel comfortable continuing to bring my children here.

As a parent, seeing a lifeguard appearing to sleep while responsible for watching children is extremely concerning. I understand there may be circumstances I’m not aware of, and I don’t want to make assumptions about the individual. But when someone is responsible for supervising children in a pool, they need to be alert and attentive. Things can happen in a matter of seconds and knowing that a lifeguard may not be fully attentive while my child and other children are swimming is not something I can simply overlook.

I’ve also noticed that many of the lifeguards appear to be younger or still in school. I understand that young people and students make up a large part of the city pools we’ve been to. So if staff are becoming too tired to remain alert during later hours, maybe management could consider whether an earlier pool schedule or different arrangements could help ensure lifeguards are rested and able to properly perform their responsibilities. Whatever the solution may be, I just want to know that the staffing and schedule are being looked at with the safety of the children in mind.

I actually tried to speak with someone at the pool about this last week, but each time I came in, the front desk and office were unattended, so I wasn’t able to find a manager or someone I could directly bring my concerns to. That is why I’m submitting this here and hoping it reaches someone who can properly look into the situation.

It is especially disappointing because we really enjoyed the facility and wanted this to be a place where our children could spend time and participate in activities. But if this continues, we will have to seriously reconsider bringing our children to the pool and I certainly cannot feel comfortable having my child continue on the swim team if I don’t feel confident that the pool is being properly supervised.

I sincerely hope management will look into this promptly and take whatever steps are necessary to make sure the pool is being properly supervised. As a parent, I should not have to question whether my child is safe while participating in an activity that is supposed to be supervised by trained lifeguards. I would really appreciate seeing this addressed before something potentially preventable happens.

description: Arlington St is dangerous for pedestrians crossing & for cars. It gets a lot of commuting traffic & cars frequently blow through the stop signs. The city often sends police units to watch the intersection of Arlington & S Hobart. Recently, speed humps were added to Faneuil St, Goodenough St, and Parsons St. We would like for speed humps to be added to Arlington St as well. A high school student was hit by a car this summer on Arlington St. We hope speed humps will prevent future accidents like this.

It has been approximately two weeks since the roadway on Talbot Avenue, between Wells Avenue and Dorchester Avenue, was milled in preparation for repaving, yet no further work appears to have been completed.

The prolonged delay is creating significant issues for neighborhood residents, including excessive dust, poor air quality, and parking difficulties.

I have respiratory problems, and the amount of dust being kicked up by passing vehicles has made it difficult for me to walk along the street, wait at the bus stop, or even enjoy my own home. I live on the third floor, and the dust is so excessive that I cannot comfortably open my windows or sit outside on my porch.

This is not just an inconvenience; it is a public health and quality-of-life concern, particularly for residents with respiratory conditions, children, and older adults.

I understand that roadwork can cause temporary disruptions, but leaving a heavily traveled residential roadway in this condition for weeks without completing the repaving is unacceptable.

I am requesting an update on when the roadway will be repaved and what immediate measures the City will take to control the dust and minimize the impact on residents until the work is completed.

description:
I would like to report an ongoing safety concern involving a large Doberman dog that repeatedly escapes from a residential property on 40 chesterfield st due to what appears to be a gate latch that’s broken or not secure. 

This is not an isolated incident. The dog gets loose frequently, and the owners have not addressed the issue. On multiple occasions I’ve seen the dog loose, running in the street when I’ve been out walking my dog. The dog has come at me while persistently barking loudly but he’s never tried to attack us.  He’s clearly had opportunities to attack and hasn’t but who knows what could happen if he got closer and was scared. His behavior seems more territorial and intimidating. 

Today we saw the dog escape and cross the street, running directly at a family with their dog and small children. He stopped as the couple was screaming at him and he ran back across the street to head towards another couple with a dog before eventually going back to his yard. 

Someone approached the residence but the owners didn’t seem too concerned he got out again. They’re aware of how often he gets out and haven’t done anything to stop it. 

My primary concern is that this continues to happen and could eventually result in someone getting hurt, a confrontation between dogs, or the Doberman being struck by a vehicle. I worry about the dogs’ safety itself along with other residents and their dogs. 

This is no fault on the dog but I’m asking that animal control please investigate this recurring issue and take appropriate steps to ensure the owners properly contain their dog so he’s not able to continuously escape their yard.

description: I submitted 101006756231 about 15 days ago, after I saw a rat in the yard at 3 Islington Ter. Inspector's reply said no activity was found. Since then, I spoke with several Islington Terrace neighbors. One saw a large rat in the 3 Islington Ter. yard last week, in the middle of the day! The rat was very bold and not intimidated by people. Another Terrace neighbor said she sees lots of rats at 3 Islington Ter. and a saw big rat on the back deck. She said the tenants seem to use the back deck as a dining area. They leave food out, and she said she's seeing more rats than before. She regularly walks her dog, so she's in and out of the house more often than we are, and out in the evening hours. The new residents also regularly leave trash in the front yard of 3 Islington Ter., which another neighbor admitted she's picking up. Since the property changed ownership, there are seem to be a lot more unrelated people living there and they seem to come and go (unsure of the leasing situation and if it's a boarding house.) It definitely seems more transitory in the past. As always, thanks so much.

description: resubmittign case BCS-00350634: Formal Housing Complaint: Defective Heating Controls, Inadequate Temperature Regulation, and Quality-of-Life Concerns Unreasonable Heating-System Operation and Continuous Tenant Burden The forced-air heating system repeatedly alternates between delivering warm air and blowing cold air into my apartment. As the apartment warms, the system subsequently circulates cold air, causing the indoor environment to become cold again. This defeats the purpose of providing heat. Instead of maintaining a reasonably warm indoor environment, the system creates a recurring cycle of heating and cooling. The existing controls offer only HIGH, LOW, and OFF settings, with no AUTO setting. I am expected to repeatedly monitor the system and decide when to turn it off or back on, without knowing when warm air will resume. Turning it off may prevent cold airflow but may also cause me to miss the next heating cycle. This is not a reasonable way to maintain indoor comfort throughout the heating season. I cannot be expected to race against the heating system 24 hours a day, seven days a week, for approximately five months each year. I request an independent inspection of the heating equipment, blower operation, and control system to determine why cold air continues to circulate between heating cycles and whether the system is operating properly under Massachusetts housing regulations, including 105 CMR 410.160 and 410.180. I request that the property owner correct any confirmed violations and remedy any defective equipment or controls responsible for the problem. | Any children under 6 years of age: [No]

311 Request Description

ANTHONY MEEKS RESIDENT/VOLUNTEER COMMUNITY ADVOCATE FOR UPHAMS CORNER COMMUNITY, DORCHESTER, BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS
EMAIL: ANTHONYMEEKS41@YAHOO.COM
COMMENDATION & ACCOMMODATION REPORT
DEPARTMENT: BOSTON PUBLIC HEALTH COMMISSION (BPHC)
TARGET UNIT: MOBILE SHARPS TEAM ("RED DOGS") / NEEDLE RECOVERY TEAM
LOCATION OF IMPACT: UPHAMS CORNER, DORCHESTER
DESCRIPTION OF EXCELLENCE:
I am submitting this official commendation and accommodation request to recognize the outstanding public safety and public health services provided by Clinton and the BPHC Mobile Sharps Needle Recovery Team (affectionately known as the "Red Dogs").
As a dedicated resident and volunteer community advocate for Uphams Corner, I witness firsthand the daily, hazardous challenges of municipal upkeep and the critical necessity of proactive substance abuse outreach. While structural leadership across municipal agencies often falters, the frontline workers of the Mobile Sharps Team demonstrate unparalleled dedication, bravery, and professionalism.
Day in and day out, these workers venture into our public squares, streets, and community flower beds to safely recover discarded needles, directly protecting our most vulnerable populations—including seniors, students, and the visually or physically challenged. Their swift, tireless intervention ensures that our community spaces remain safe for children to play without the terror of biohazards.
The everyday employees of the Needle Recovery Team are hardworking, blameless, and deeply empathetic to the plight of Dorchester residents. Clinton and the entire crew represent the finest foundation of community-oriented public servitude. Their tireless efforts mitigate local hazards, restore neighborhood dignity, and save lives. They deserve the highest city accolades, sustainable program funding, and deep administrative recognition.
Thank you, Mobile Sharps Team, for your unwavering commitment to Uphams Corner.
SUBMITTED BY:
ANTHONY MEEKS
RESIDENT/VOLUNTEER COMMUNITY ADVOCATE FOR UPHAMS CORNER COMMUNITY NO NEIGHBORHOOD BOSTON
EMAIL: ANTHONYMEEKS41@YAHOO.COM

description:
Location: Intersection of Nonantum Road, Greenough Boulevard, and N Beacon Street.

Issue: Unsafe pedestrian crossing signals.

The pedestrian crossing signals at this intersection appear to allow pedestrians to safely cross only one direction of traffic at a time. After crossing one section of the road, pedestrians are left waiting in the middle of the intersection without a clear signal indicating when it is safe to cross the other direction.

This creates a dangerous situation for pedestrians, as they are forced to wait in the middle of the roadway while trying to determine when it is safe to continue crossing.

Recently, I saw a young boy on his bicycle who was stranded on one side of the intersection and unable to safely cross. I had to go back and help him. This incident highlighted how dangerous and confusing this crossing can be, especially for children.

Request: Please inspect this intersection and review the pedestrian crossing signals to ensure that pedestrians and cyclists can safely cross the entire intersection without being stranded in the middle of the road. Appropriate signal adjustments or other safety improvements are urgently needed to prevent a potential accident.

description:
Requesting an all-way stop at the intersection of Sumner St and S Bremen St in East Boston.

Currently only S Bremen St has a stop sign. Cars are consistently parked along both sides of Sumner St right up to the intersection, which blocks the view of oncoming traffic for drivers stopped on S Bremen. Drivers have to creep into Sumner St without being able to see what's coming, which feels blind and dangerous. The intersection also feels like the top of a small hill, which adds to the challenge.

There is also steady foot traffic at this intersection, so pedestrians are crossing in front of confused drivers who can't see well.

I've lived nearby for almost two years and this is a daily problem. I'm requesting that BTD review this intersection for:
1. An all-way stop (stop signs on Sumner St)
2. Updated/refreshed crosswalk paint
3. No-parking zones near the corners to improve sightlines

A traffic signal would also be welcome if the intersection qualifies. Thank you.

description:
To: Boston City Hall, Boston Parks and Recreation Department, and the Appropriate Boston City Council Representatives

We, the undersigned residents and supporters of Talbot Avenue and the surrounding community, respectfully petition the City of Boston to consider establishing a standard-size, enclosed dog area for local residents and their dogs that are unable to walk the distance to Ronan park which is a 39 minute walk from Talbot Avenue where many dog owners reside. 

Our Request

We request that the City of Boston explore the feasibility of designating and developing a suitable space along Talbot Avenue for a fenced, enclosed dog area where residents can safely exercise their dogs, encourage healthy interaction, and connect with fellow members of the community.

Why This Matters

1. Promoting Healthy Movement and Dog Socialization

Dogs need regular physical activity, stimulation, and appropriate opportunities to interact with other dogs. A designated, enclosed area would provide a more controlled environment for exercise and socialization, while allowing owners to supervise their pets responsibly.

2. Strengthening Our Community

A neighborhood dog area is more than a space for pets. It is an opportunity for neighbors to meet, build friendships, exchange support, and develop a stronger sense of belonging. This small but meaningful improvement could help create a more connected, welcoming, and engaged community.

3. Supporting Responsible Dog Ownership

A designated area with secure fencing, controlled entry gates, waste-disposal facilities, and clear usage guidelines would encourage responsible pet ownership and provide an appropriate place for permitted off-leash activity.

4. Investing in a Healthier Neighborhood

Access to shared recreational spaces encourages residents to spend more time outdoors, stay active, and participate in neighborhood life. A thoughtfully planned dog area would be a practical investment in the well-being of residents and their pets.

Our Commitment to a Thoughtful Solution

We recognize the importance of responsible planning, neighborhood input, public safety, accessibility, cleanliness, and consideration for nearby residents. We ask the city to assess potential locations, available public land, maintenance requirements, and the level of community support for this proposal.

We believe that meaningful community improvements do not always require large investments. Sometimes, a modest change can create lasting benefits for the people and animals who call a neighborhood home.

description:
I am submitting a formal complaint regarding the unacceptable and unprofessional trash collection service on Saratoga Street in East Boston.

Due to Monday’s holiday, trash collection was pushed back by one day, with pickup expected on Wednesday, October 14. However, while the opposite side of Saratoga Street had its trash collected, multiple houses on our side of the street were completely skipped.

This is absolutely unacceptable. Residents followed the adjusted collection schedule and placed their trash outside as instructed, only for sanitation workers to leave an entire section of the street without service.

This is not just an inconvenience. It is a serious sanitation concern. Residents already have significant amounts of household waste, and leaving trash uncollected creates the potential for overflowing bins, foul odors, rodents, pests, and unsanitary conditions around people’s homes.

It is extremely frustrating that one side of the street received service while the other was neglected. Residents should not have to suffer because of inconsistent or incomplete collection services. We pay taxes and expect basic city services to be performed properly and professionally.

I am requesting immediate trash collection for all affected properties on Saratoga Street, along with an explanation as to why multiple homes were skipped. I also request that this issue be reviewed with the sanitation department to prevent it from happening again.

Leaving residents with accumulating garbage is unacceptable, unsanitary, and demonstrates a serious lack of accountability. This situation needs to be corrected immediately, not left unresolved until the next scheduled collection day.

You can:
·         File online: Mass.gov Consumer Complaint Form — upload receipts, photos, and other documents.

·         By mail:
Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Advocacy & Response Division
One Ashburton Place, 18th Floor
Boston, MA 02108

·         By phone: Call the Consumer Hotline at (617) 727-8400 for guidance or to request a form. The AGO can mediate, refer you to local programs, or use your complaint in broader enforcement actions.

Thank you!

description:
EMERGENCY MUNICIPAL INFRASTRUCTURE COMPLAINT & HIGH-SEVERITY PUBLIC SAFETY REPORT
LOCATION METADATA: 531 Columbia Road (Frugal Furniture Building Block), Uphams Corner, Dorchester, MA 02125
DEPARTMENT ROUTING: Inspectional Services Department (ISD) / Fire Prevention Command
BOS:311 CASE RE-ACTIVATION ID: #1016764013

CRITICAL CRIME AND POLICE INFILTRATION NARRATIVE:
The absolute catastrophic risk of leaving this commercial perimeter breached has been empirically proven by a massive recent emergency escalation at this exact location. A dangerous criminal suspect successfully bypassed the unsecured structural boundary and barricaded themselves directly inside that open high-voltage utility closet. This high-intensity crisis forced an overwhelming containment perimeter consisting of a rapid-response grid of approximately 6 to 8 Boston Police District B-2 marked cruisers, specialized investigative detective units, precinct lieutenants, and multiple sector sergeants to descend on the property to coordinate a tactical extraction and subsequent arrest within the high-voltage perimeter. This was an intense, high-risk operations event caused entirely by a reckless refusal to lock a door.

LANDLORD DECEPTION & ON-SITE HAZARDS:
Direct field intervention was taken to personally confront the building property manager and landlord regarding this dangerous perimeter breach. The landlord provided explicit, verbal assurances that this commercial structure would be physically sealed and legally secured by the end of the night. The landlord lied. Year to date, this high-voltage utility closet remains entirely unsecured and unlatched because of the landlord's outright, negligent refusal to lock the perimeter door. This failure permits unauthorized individuals, vagrants, and drug addicts continuous, uninhibited access to the live high-voltage equipment. Photographic evidence from physical field audits reveals an active tinderbox; left scattered on the floor directly adjacent to high-voltage equipment is an unregulated heating element alongside substantial piles of flammable candle wax.

DIMINISHED QUALITY OF LIFE & IMPACT ON LOCAL ANCHORS:
This unmonitored room sits at the absolute physical foundation of a block of commercial merchants that serve as the vital economic anchor of our neighborhood. Critically, there are occupied residential apartments located directly above this unsecured fire hazard. Leaving this high-voltage area breached creates a severe, diminished quality of life, an unbearable atmosphere of fear, and a catastrophic liability for our neighborhood.

DEADLY CONSEQUENCES DECLARATION:
We are facing an active, impending fire catastrophe and severe neighborhood havoc as a direct consequence of municipal neglect and landlord deception. If a barricaded criminal can exploit this unsecured asset to hide, any individual can access it to cause havoc or set it ablaze—threatening the structural foundation of the commercial anchor and risking a devastating, deadly multi-alarm fire that will cause a catastrophic partial roof collapse, permanently injuring or killing local merchant families, patrons, and innocent children. We refuse to stand by and watch our neighborhood suffer due to an absolute oversight and a negligent refusal to lock this perimeter. Immediate emergency municipal enforcement, proactive structural remediation, and strict penal code fines must be executed to protect the traveling public, local merchants, and the diverse Black and Brown families of the Uphams Corner community.

description:
I am writing to formally report misleading and incomplete street parking signage at this location, which directly resulted in unfair ticketing for multiple drivers today , A street, near melcher and necco.

Inaccurate/Incomplete Street Signage: The posted sign directly in front of where I parked explicitly states "2 Hour Parking - Pay via ParkBoston." There is zero mention or indication anywhere on this sign that a residential permit or special permit is required. If permit restrictions apply here, clear and visible signage stating "Permit Only during xx hours" or specific permit hours must be installed immediately.

Misleading ParkBoston App Instructions: When attempting to verify restrictions via the ParkBoston app, the app simply directs users to "Look for posted signage." Following this instruction leads directly to the incomplete sign on the street, creating a trap for drivers who are actively attempting to comply with city rules. Its also not helpful that there is A parking meter that says no payment is required at this time, how many confusing messages are these?

Widespread Confusion: This is not an isolated oversight. At least two other vehicles parked behind me received tickets at the same time for the exact same reason. The parking enforcement officer was standing right at the location capitalizing on this confusion rather than addressing the obvious gap in signage with the city. I spoke with him and he AGREED on the confusing signage as well. Later he proceeded to show me a sign that was placed at the beginning of the street. So the city is expecting me not only to read the 4 signs but also walk around the block to make sure no other signs apply?? Move the signage to the same post as the others if thats what the issue is.

Please fix the sign, 60$ of a fine from anyone who doesnt live in the area and doesnt know any better is ridiculous.

description:
BOSTON TRANSPORTATION DEPARTMENT
Resident Parking Program Division
1 City Hall Square, Room 721
Boston, MA 02201

SUBJECT: Formal Request for Resident Permit Parking Evaluation – Dorchester, MA

To the Boston Transportation Department Resident Parking Division,

I am writing as a full-time resident of Dorchester to formally request a neighborhood parking evaluation for our block to convert it from an unrestricted parking zone into a designated Resident Permit Parking Only zone. 

Our street consists entirely of high-density triple-decker homes. Because these residential properties lack driveways or off-street parking facilities, the on-street curb space is a vital resource for the residents who live here. Unfortunately, this finite resource is currently being severely overwhelmed due to our direct proximity to local commercial businesses (specifically a local pizza restaurant and nail salon).

We regularly face severe parking congestion caused by a combination of:
1. Commercial Overflow: Patrons and delivery drivers from the adjacent commercial lot frequently utilize our residential street for short-term and long-term parking, creating high-turnover traffic, double-parking hazards, and neighborhood friction.
2. Space Hoarding & Neighbor Conflict: Because the street is entirely unrestricted, some households are weaponizing the public curb by shuffling multiple idle vehicles to hoard spaces, forcing residents with severe mobility impairments to regularly park multiple blocks away from their homes.

This ongoing commercial overflow and lack of regulation has significantly degraded the quality of life, safety, and accessibility on our block. Introducing a Resident Permit Parking restriction would protect the neighborhood, ensure that spaces are preserved for the people who actually live here, and deter commercial patrons from treating our residential street as an auxiliary parking lot.

I kindly request that BTD dispatch an enforcement or engineering representative to assess the parking density and commercial overflow on our block, and provide the necessary petition guidelines so we can begin gathering signatures from our neighbors.

Thank you for your time, consideration, and dedication to keeping Boston's residential neighborhoods accessible.

Sincerely, Molly Jennings, 7 Semont Road, Unit 1, Dorchester, MA 02124

description: -- auto translated (en-US) -- Hello, I am requesting a housing inspection due to an ongoing rodent issue affecting my apartment. We discovered what appears to be a dead rodent inside a wall vent, which has caused an increasingly unbearable decomposition odor throughout our apartment. The smell has spread from the hallway into our bathroom, living room, kitchen area, bedrooms, and closets. It has permeated our clothing and belongings to the point that the odor is noticeable even when we leave the apartment. We have also experienced flies inside the apartment, and I have had to temporarily relocate my young son to his grandmother’s home because of the conditions. Management arranged for pest control, but the technician spent approximately two minutes in our apartment and advised that nothing could be done except wait for the odor to dissipate. He also informed me that management was already aware of rodent problems in two upstairs units, including an opening reportedly allowing mice into the walls. I have photographic evidence of the suspected rodent (keep in mind we found more than 1) and written correspondence documenting my attempts to resolve this with management. I am requesting an inspection to assess the sanitary conditions in our apartment and determine whether the reported rodent infestation and entry points are being appropriately addressed. Thank you for your assistance. -- original (en-US) -- Hello, I am requesting a housing inspection due to an ongoing rodent issue affecting my apartment. description:
Subject: Formal Health Complaint – Barcelona Wine Bar, 1700 Beacon Street

Dear Health Department,

I am writing to formally report potential food safety and sanitation violations observed at Barcelona Wine Bar, located at 1700 Beacon Street.

During my visit, I observed two mice in the dining area moving toward the kitchen. The presence of rodents in an area where food is served raises serious concerns about sanitation, possible food contamination, and the restaurant’s pest-control practices.

Additionally, I observed staff members handling soiled dishes removed from dining tables and then proceeding to cut bread without washing their hands in between. This raised concerns about proper hand hygiene and the potential for cross-contamination of food.

These observations raise serious concerns regarding the establishment’s compliance with applicable food safety, sanitation, pest-control, and employee handwashing requirements.

I respectfully request that the Health Department investigate these concerns and conduct an inspection to determine whether corrective action is necessary to protect public health.

I am submitting this complaint in the interest of public health and the safety of customers who dine at this establishment. I appreciate your prompt attention to this matter and request that appropriate action be taken if violations are confirmed.

Thank you for your time and attention.

Sincerely,

A Concerned Customer

Management has been notified repeatedly over the past month. They have sent multiple emails acknowledging that the heating system is entirely broken, but they continue to issue empty updates with no meaningful progress or clear timeline for when the heat will be restored. They are attempting to bypass code regulations by telling residents to just "ask for a space heater" rather than fixing the primary heating system. description:
-- auto translated (en-US) -- Dear City of Boston Officials, Thank you for all the great service you provide.  I am writing to request immediate action on the persistent rat infestation in Allston–Brighton, with particular concern for Lower Allston, the residential neighborhood north of I-90 and south of the Charles River. While rodent control is important throughout Allston–Brighton, I want to specifically draw attention to Lower Allston, where families with young children live and where residents should be able to walk, play, and enjoy their neighborhood without encountering rats. Rats are frequently visible on sidewalks, near homes, and around trash collection areas. This is a serious public health and sanitation concern, particularly in a residential neighborhood where children regularly spend time outdoors. I urge the city to take coordinated action, particularly in Lower Allston, including: 1. Targeted rodent extermination and treatment along residential streets, alleys, and known infestation hotspots. 2. City-provided, rodent-resistant trash containers rather than placing the financial burden entirely on individual residents and landlords. 3. Stricter sanitation enforcement for properties and businesses contributing to rodent activity. 4. Regular inspections and follow-up treatments to ensure measurable and lasting improvements. Simply asking residents to report individual sightings or purchase better trash bins is not an adequate solution to a neighborhood-wide infestation. This requires a coordinated municipal response. description:
I am submitting yet another complaint about the dumpsters on Seaview Ave.

As I was turning the corner onto Drumlin, I could smell these dumpsters from several meters away. The smell is overwhelming and has become an issue for the surrounding neighborhood. Once again, the dumpsters are overflowing, with trash and waste spilling into the surrounding area.

The street and sidewalks are covered in years of staining and buildup from the liquids leaking out of these dumpsters. The amount of leakage onto public property is disgusting and creates a potential health hazard for the children, residents, and pets who walk these sidewalks every day.

At what point are those responsible going to be held accountable? How many complaints need to be filed before the City actually takes meaningful action?

This has been going on for years. The smell, overflowing trash, and waste leaking onto public property are completely unacceptable. Residents should not have to continuously complain about something as basic as sanitation in their own neighborhood.

I am fed up and disgusted with how the City has handled this issue. Temporary cleanups are clearly not working, and the conditions continue to return.

I want to know what is actually being done to hold the responsible parties accountable and what the City plans to do to permanently address this issue. Enough is enough.

description:
I am filing yet another complaint regarding the overflowing dumpsters on Seaview Avenue and the ongoing unsanitary conditions affecting the surrounding neighborhood.

My previous complaint, BCS-00357802, was closed with the explanation that it had been “relocated to a Non-City of Boston Stakeholder.” What exactly does that mean? Who was this complaint referred to, and what action has actually been taken?

These dumpsters continue to overflow, produce overwhelming odors, and leak waste onto the surrounding sidewalks and streets. The staining and buildup from years of leakage are clearly visible on public property. This is not simply an issue involving private dumpsters. It is an ongoing sanitation problem affecting an entire neighborhood.

The street and sidewalks also need to be thoroughly washed, sprayed down, and sanitized. Years of leaking garbage, waste, and filthy runoff have created an unacceptable buildup of potentially hazardous residue on public property. Simply emptying the dumpsters does nothing to address the years of contamination left behind. The surrounding pavement needs a proper deep cleaning, not another temporary fix.

I understand that the dumpsters may be privately owned, but the sidewalks and streets are public property. Residents, children, and pets walk through this area daily. How can the city continue to close these complaints without ensuring that the conditions are actually addressed?

I am requesting an inspection by the Inspectional Services Department, a thorough cleaning and sanitization of the affected streets and sidewalks, an explanation of why my previous complaint was closed, and clarification on what enforcement measures are being taken against the responsible property owner or waste management company.

I am beyond frustrated with the city’s handling of this issue. Referring a complaint to another party is not a resolution. These conditions have persisted for years, and someone needs to be held accountable. I would appreciate an actual response outlining what is being done to correct this problem rather than another case being closed without any visible improvement.

description:
On October 20, 2026, I paid at the multi-space pay-by-plate kiosk with machine ID 600801154 on Charles Street, on the block between Boylston Street and Beacon Street beside the Public Garden. My paid session ran from 1:05 PM to 2:41 PM, and the City’s electronic receipt shows the correct plate number. 

My car, parked on that same block, nevertheless received violation number 842504808 for “Meter Fee Unpaid” at 1:53 PM, in the middle of the paid session. 

This ticket was issued wrongfully, and it raises serious concerns about the reliability of the new pay-by-plate system, especially because the kiosks give no physical receipt and drivers who paid correctly may assume the mistake was theirs and simply pay the fine. The ticket lists the meter number as “dd001,” which does not match the kiosk where I paid. This suggests that payments made at this kiosk are not reaching enforcement officers’ devices, or are being recorded against the wrong block. Please investigate how this kiosk is linked to enforcement so that other drivers who pay correctly are not ticketed. I have filed a separate appeal for the violation itself.

In Kenmore Sq on Commonwealth Ave, taking a Left turn onto Brookline Ave is very challenging as a cyclist. I bike to work each morning and there are extremely faded lines of a bike lane adjacent to the Left turn lane on Com Ave as I head towards Fenway. There is more than enough room at the intersection for both motorists and cyclists, but cyclists need to have the bike lane repainted so the cars can respect our designated space as we wait to turn. This single turn of my commute is easily the most dangerous part and one I dread each day, on what is otherwise a mostly pleasant ride. Completion of this simple request would mean so much to myself and other cyclists who feel unsafe at this intersection. description:
ISD. 

Blocking sidewalk.

I am writing to urge the City to investigate pedestrian safety at the intersection of Union Street and Chestnut Hill Avenue in Brighton and consider installing a pedestrian-activated crossing signal or other appropriate safety measures.

There is currently a marked crosswalk at this intersection, but vehicles frequently travel through the area at high speeds, making it extremely difficult and dangerous for pedestrians to cross safely. I live nearby and have personally witnessed several instances in which pedestrians have nearly been struck by cars while attempting to use the crosswalk.

This is particularly concerning because the intersection is heavily used by children and families. There are schools nearby, and Union Street is a common walking route for children traveling to area schools, the library, the park, and other neighborhood destinations. A painted crosswalk alone does not seem sufficient given the speed of traffic and the number of pedestrians who rely on this crossing.

I am asking the City to please conduct a safety assessment of this intersection, including vehicle speeds, traffic volume, pedestrian use, and visibility, and determine whether a pedestrian-activated flashing beacon, signal, traffic-calming measures, or other improvements are warranted.

This feels like an opportunity to address a clear safety hazard before someone is seriously injured. I would greatly appreciate the City investigating the intersection and letting neighborhood residents know what steps can be taken to make this crossing safer.

Thank you for your attention to this issue.

description:
Construction project at 11.5 Union Park causing constant issues w parking on our block—illegal parking, impeding traffic etc. Project has 3x resident spots w 7day a week, 7am-4pm permits, yet still every day there are at a number of more vehicles on site, parked illegally often for most of the day.  Double parked, parked at median etc, often impeding traffic around the median, cutting off the two way traffic, blocking hydrant, or blocking in resident spots. Today as example, photos attached, multiple double parked vehicles, one 
at median fully blocking any ability to drive around median. I’ve witnessed many instances of people blocked in, long backups with constant honking, trucks trying to maneuver around and hitting the park fence, near accidents.  Any approach to people in the vehicles to move or at least have some courtesy been met with aggressive behavior.  Today I called BPD, D-4, on the non-emergency line and was told that no one would come look at it, that no action would be taken as it was ‘not an emergency, and we have better things to do.’ At 2pm on a Tuesday. No community policing, or traffic enforcement effort whatsoever.  I’d like to know who in the City intends to do any sort of parking or code enforcement, since all of the relevant agencies don’t seem interested. This project has been causing these issues for over a year at this point, with no end soon.

Subject: Request to Repair or Replace Streetlights in Our Neighborhood

Dear City of Boston 311 Team,

I am writing to request that the city inspect and repair or replace the streetlights in our neighborhood. The area is very dark at night due to poor street lighting, which makes residents and families feel unsafe, especially children walking in the neighborhood.

We are concerned about the safety of our children and all residents. Better lighting would help prevent accidents and improve public safety.

Please send a team to inspect the streetlights and take the necessary action as soon as possible.

Thank you for your attention and assistance.

While rodent control is important throughout Allston–Brighton, I want to specifically draw attention to Lower Allston, where families with young children live and where residents should be able to walk, play, and enjoy their neighborhood without encountering rats. This is a serious public health and sanitation concern, particularly in a residential neighborhood where children regularly spend time outdoors. I urge the city to take coordinated action, particularly in Lower Allston. Simply asking residents to report individual sightings or purchase better trash bins is not an adequate solution to a neighborhood-wide infestation. This requires a coordinated municipal response. I urge the city to take coordinated action, particularly in Lower Allston.

Simply asking residents to report individual sightings or purchase better trash bins is not an adequate solution to a neighborhood-wide infestation. This requires a coordinated municipal response.

description:
Request for Street Lighting Assessment & Improvements – Rogers Park, Brighton

I am a Brighton resident requesting an evaluation of the existing street lighting surrounding Rogers Park, particularly along the park’s perimeter and adjacent residential streets.

During the warmer months, the tennis courts and baseball fields provide supplemental lighting to the surrounding area. However, once the athletic season ends and those lights are no longer in use, the surrounding streets and sidewalks become extremely dark, creating significant visibility and pedestrian safety concerns.

As an expecting first-time mom and dog owner who regularly walks through the neighborhood, I am particularly concerned about navigating these areas after sunset, especially during the fall and winter months when daylight hours are shorter. This is a year-round community safety concern that affects dog walkers, families, runners, and other residents.

I have been in direct communication with Boston Parks & Recreation regarding the upcoming Rogers Park improvements. While additional pedestrian security lighting is being considered, construction funding is not expected until FY2028.

Boston Parks & Recreation specifically directed me to submit a 311 request so that Public Works can evaluate the street lighting in this area.

I am formally requesting that Public Works assess the current lighting conditions surrounding Rogers Park and explore opportunities to install additional streetlights or implement interim lighting improvements before 2028.

I would appreciate an update on whether an assessment can be conducted and what near-term solutions may be available to address these safety concerns.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

I am reporting a recurring pigeon-feeding problem at this location of valenti way and canal st. I personally witness the woman who regularly stays in this area feeding a very large number of pigeons everyday at approximately 11:00 AM. There were well over 100 pigeons gathered around her and the food, spread across multiple areas of the sidewalk and street. This is not an isolated occurrence. I have observed this same woman feeding pigeons repeatedly and believe this occurs nearly every day, generally after she gets up in the morning. I have previously observed her feeding them around 10AM - 12pm and have now documented it again at approximately 11 AM. The feeding is attracting hundreds of pigeons to the intersection and surrounding North Station pedestrian area. The birds leave substantial droppings on the sidewalk, railings and surrounding areas, and food is left on the ground, creating a sanitation concern and potentially attracting rodents. I have attached photographs taken today showing the woman actively feeding the pigeons and the large number of pigeons gathered around her. There has already been a 311 complaint regarding a woman feeding pigeons at this exact intersection. That complaint was closed after an inspector visited on July 17, 2026 but did not observe anyone feeding the pigeons. The feeding is recurring, so I am specifically requesting that an inspector visit during the morning hours when this activity is occurring. Please investigate this recurring pigeon-feeding activity and the resulting sanitation conditions.
